intro: Beneath your feet lie thirty-three cities, one on top of another. You are at Yumuktepe, a mound in Mersin province reaching back to 7000 BC. With thirty-three settlement layers, it is one of the longest continuously inhabited mounds in the world, and its Chalcolithic walls are among the earliest fortifications known.
history: This mound inside the city of Mersin holds thirty-three settlement layers reaching back to 7000 BC, making it one of the longest continuously occupied places on earth. John Garstang dug it in the 1930s; Turkish and Italian teams followed from the 1990s. And its Chalcolithic wall and gate system is among the earliest fortifications known anywhere.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Chalcolithic wall and gate, think of the thirty-three layers beneath you, and look for the Neolithic houses and the Hittite level.
facts: Did you know? The Chalcolithic walls mark the moment defensive building passes from village to fortress: by 5000 BC there was a walled circuit here, with a gate and towers. And with thirty-three settlement layers, Yumuktepe is among the longest continuously inhabited places on earth, its lowest reaching to 7000 BC.
outro: This brings our journey through Yumuktepe to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These layers have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
